title: 19th-Century Medical Revolution Adventure

concepts.def: Proved cholera spread by water in Soho, 1854
1867 used carbolic acid as an antiseptic in surgery
Reformed nursing and hospital hygiene from 1854
1875 Act forced councils to provide clean water

walkthroughs.body_html:
In 1796 Edward Jenner noticed milkmaids who caught cowpox did not get smallpox.

He tested the idea on James Phipps and published his findings in 1798. In 1853 vaccination was made compulsory for babies.

In 1854 John Snow mapped cholera deaths around the Broad Street pump in Soho.

He removed the pump handle and deaths fell. In 1861 Louis Pasteur published Germ Theory — proving microbes, not miasma, cause disease.

In 1867 Joseph Lister used carbolic acid spray in surgery — deaths from infection plummeted.

Florence Nightingale's hygiene reforms cut hospital death rates. Parliament passed the 1875 Public Health Act, forcing councils to provide clean water and sewers.
